notes: [SPECTRAL: LED 3000K share 46-90% (Phase 1 done Jan 2026; Phase 2 due end-2026); point at the plan's 60%. mel-DER/blue/DNB are lumen-weighted mixes of measured lamp-class medians (lamp_class_reference.csv).] CCT: Beijing's 15th Five-Year (2026-2030) urban lighting plan (published Sept 2025, loaded) says road lighting uses '3000K warm white as the main tone', with lower CCT on the Central Axis and historic areas and higher CCT allowed in modern business districts. Its colour-zoning table defines W = warm yellow <3300K and C = 3300-5300K. This is a plan and policy statement. The procurement pages I could read (DRC approval 京发改(审)〔2024〕365号, 2024-06-06; OPPLE lot-01 award, 2024-12-24, CNY 21.8M) put the fixture specs in attachments I could not see, so no fixture-level CCT was verified. STOCK: the central city has about 306,000 municipal road lamps, historically HPS plus metal halide. Phase 1 replaced about 141,500 HPS lamps with modular LED on 2,488 roads outside the 4th Ring (including the 4th Ring main and auxiliary roads) and some roads between the 3rd and 4th Rings. It started late 2024 and was reported complete in Jan 2026 (about 46% of central-city lamps). Phase 2 (about 55,000 lamps inside the 3rd Ring plus the Chang'an Ave and Central Axis extensions) launched 2025-12-15, with all work due by end-2026. Tencent News (Sept 2026) reports 2,146 HPS sets on Chang'an Ave and its extensions, the 2nd/3rd Rings and Qianmen already converted by Aug 2026, with CCT 'carefully designed' to keep a 'solemn, elegant' look (no K value given). LED SHARE: the plan says the central city is 'still mainly sodium lamps' with an energy-saving luminaire rate of only 60%, and sets a city-wide LED target of 60% to 90%. The 60% figure is a 2025 statement and it is unclear whether it includes Phase 1. By late 2026 central-city LED is probably well above 60% but unquantified. MEASURED: SDGSAT-1 first images (released 2021-12-20, thepaper) show the main urban area dominated by warm yellow HPS, and the sub-centre, Yizhuang, Daxing, Fangshan, Shijingshan and east Changping dominated by LED. Applied Energy 2023 SDGSAT-1 paper (S0306261923017191): Beijing >50% LED lighting in 2022. That is snippet-only (paywalled) and conflicts with the plan's 'mainly sodium' statement, so treat it as approximate. Suburban LEDs installed before 2024 (pre-plan) are likely cooler (4000K+), but this is not verified.

Greater Santiago is ~35+ comunas each running its own lighting, so there is no single city stock. Comuna de Santiago (the centre): 37,054 luminaires; plan announced Nov 2020 to replace 23,500 (63%) old sodium with LED by 1H-2021; earlier LED on Alameda/Vicuna Mackenna/Matta/San Francisco in 2017 and Barrio Yungay in 2019; GORE RM put in 4,191 LED in Santiago Centro (Jan 2019). So the comuna de Santiago is probably mostly LED since 2021, but no completion figure was found. Nationally, the BID 2013 inventory in the DIPRES evaluation gives ~2.42M luminaires, 77-89% HPS. The national MinEnergia recambio programme started Aug 2014 (85 comunas, 130,000 luminaires by 2017, target 200,000) and was aimed at poorer comunas. NASA Earth Observatory (ISS070-E-93399, 14 Feb 2024) shows a patchwork of orange HPS and white LED across comunas and says Maipu and El Bosque began changing lights in autumn 2023, so the metro area is still mixed. No tender or press release that states a CCT was found; the Providencia (2020) and Las Condes (2025) tender bases exist but their CCT could not be read. Regulation: DS 43/2012 covered only the observatory regions (Antofagasta, Atacama, Coquimbo; from background knowledge, not checked this session), so it did not bind Santiago. DS 1/2022 (published 18 Oct 2023, in force 19 Oct 2024) covers the whole country: outside Special Protection Areas the blue-light share is capped at 7% (1% inside them). Existing national-territory installations only need to comply at end of useful life, and new ones from 19 Oct 2026. So post-2024 installs should be warm (~3000K or lower) and pre-2024 LED may be 4000K. led_share and cct left blank on purpose.

Lots 1-2 went to UTE Luz Madrid (Sice, Urbalux, Imesapi, Etralux, Citelum) and lot 3 to UTE Inmaes (Ferrovial, FCC, Indra, Telvent). Retrofit Q4 2014 to 1H 2015 (~150,000 done by Mar 2015) covered 225,000 points. 84,000 became Philips LED: 33,000 historic 'Fernandino/Villa' lanterns got LED modules made in Valladolid, and 51,000 1990s globe luminaires were replaced with 'Quebec' LED. The other ~124,000-141,000 points only got a more efficient light source and electronic gear. The UCM thesis/paper (Robles et al. 2021) describes this as HPS 250 W/150 W reduced to 150 W/70 W, i.e. HPS kept at lower wattage. A programmed night-time power-reduction schedule plus GPRS telemanagement was also part of the design. Target was 44% lighting energy saving. The '3000 K' figure comes from a search snippet attributed to Robles et al. 2021 ('retrofits in Madrid primarily replace HPS lamps with 3000 K LEDs'). I could not open the full text (MDPI 403; the Zenodo PDF was too large), so it is snippet-only. UCM also measured HPS, 3000K and 4000K LED spectra on Madrid street poles. LED share: 35.6% in 2019 and 66.9% in 2025 out of 253,575 luminaires. 2019 matches the 84k LED installed in 2015, so there was little LED growth 2015-2019. 2022 maintenance contract: more than 71,000 discharge luminaires to LED; target at least 75% LED by 2027 (PRTR funds). Ground truth: UCM sky brightness in Johnson B fell 14% 2011-2015 and rose 32% 2015-2019. Spain's REEAE (RD 1890/2008) sets efficiency and upward-light limits, not CCT. The 2013 PPT pliego on sede.madrid.es returned 403.
